Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: TECHNOLOGY- CYBER SAFETY Suggested vocabulary to be signed: crime, trust, strang
Topic 7.1: Observing and articulating signs 7.1.1 Proper articulation of signs and vocabulary: Observing interactively
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and articulating signs 7.1.1 Proper articulation of signs and vocabulary: Observing interactively, part of TECHNOLOGY- CYBER SAFETY Suggested vocabulary to be signed: crime, trust, strang in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why should you listen to others when they are speaking? 2. Why should you observe others when they are signing and fingerspelling?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and articulating signs 7.1.1 Proper articulation of signs and vocabulary: Observing interactively together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: observing and articulating a sign clearly is enhanced as learner participates effectively in a two way

conversation with peers.

● Digital literacy: connecting with technology is developed as learner uses social media to share views on

debates and watch interviews.

Values:
● Unity: cooperation as the learner is able to collaborate with peers to perform task such as debates, interviews and role playing a dialogue.

● Respect: open mindedness is promoted as the learner is able to accommodate the views of others during debates or interviews.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate the theme of technology to their learning in Pre-technical studies.

  -  In pairs, learners are guided to watch a

captioned video clip or observe a signed

demonstration of vocabulary related to

technology.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to identify,

fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to

technology.


  -  In groups, learners who are Hard of Hearing

are guided to listen for sounds /ɛə/ /j/ /ʤ//ʒ/

from an audio text and then say them aloud

for example:

o sounds /ɛə/- share, bear, wear, care

o sounds /j/ - you, yield, yes, youtube

o sounds /ʤ/- judge, edge, job, language

o sounds /ʒ/- vision, manage, decision


  -  In pairs learners who are Deaf are guided to

observe, fingerspell and sign words with the

letter sounds /ɛə/ /j/ /ʤ//ʒ/ from a signed

audio-visual text and then sign the word

clearly, for example:

o letter sounds /ɛə/- share, bear, wear, care

o letter sounds /j/ - you, yield, yes, youtube

o letter sounds /ʤ/- judge, edge, job, language

o letter sounds /ʒ/- vision, manage, decision

  -  In groups, learners who are Hard of Hearing

are guided to listen to an introduction to a

dialogue and predict events.


  -  In groups, learners who are Deaf are guided to

observe an introduction to a signed dialogue

and predict events.


  -  In pairs or groups, learner is guided to act out

a dialogue featuring vocabulary with the

sounds /ɛə/ /j/ /ʤ//ʒ/ collaboratively.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to construct

sentences using present and past tense.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to apply facial

expressions and gestures appropriately while

reciting choral verses with peers.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to record one

another when performing a signed choral

verse or short dialogues.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to watch a

signed audio-visual recording of short

interviews and then conduct a role play with

others.


  -  In groups, learners who are Hard of Hearing

are guided to take turns during an oral

interview, discussion or debate.


  -  In groups, learners who are Deaf are guided to

take turns during a signed interview,

discussion or debate.


  -  In pairs or groups, learners are guided to

participate in a debate, signed interview or

discussion on social media.
